title: Career Roadmap · Textile Technician
summary: A Textile Technician supports the production, processing, testing and quality control of fibres, yarns, fabrics and textile products. The role combines practical knowledge of textile materials, machinery, production processes, testing procedures and workplace safety.

facts.Current degree: Diploma in Textile / Garment / Fashion Technology

about.label: Typical Entry Qualification
about.text: Diploma in Textile Technology, Textile Engineering, Garment Technology, Fashion Technology or a related discipline

about.label: Work Environments
about.text: Textile mills, spinning and weaving units, knitting factories, dyeing and finishing plants, garment manufacturers, textile testing laboratories and technical textile companies

about.label: Career Focus
about.text: Operating and monitoring textile machinery, supporting production, identifying fabric defects, conducting quality checks and maintaining equipment and process records

blocks.text: A Textile Technician supports the production, processing, testing and quality control of fibres, yarns, fabrics and textile products. The role combines practical knowledge of textile materials, machinery, production processes, testing procedures and workplace safety.
The exact responsibilities depend on the diploma specialization:

blocks.label: Textile Technology
blocks.text: spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and fabric testing.

blocks.label: Garment Technology
blocks.text: garment production, stitching operations, measurement, finishing and quality inspection.

blocks.label: Fashion Technology
blocks.text: garment construction, fabric selection, production methods and technical product development.

Entry-level positions may include Textile Production Technician, Spinning Technician, Weaving Technician, Knitting Technician, Fabric Inspection Technician or Textile Testing Assistant. With experience, technicians can progress into production supervision, quality assurance, process development or textile machinery maintenance.

rows.text: Learn textile materials, machinery, production processes and quality inspection. Enter a textile production or testing role.
Handle machine setup, process monitoring, defect analysis and routine production troubleshooting.
Specialize in textile quality, dyeing and finishing, technical textiles, production efficiency or textile testing.
Potentially progress into Senior Textile Technician, Production Supervisor, Quality Manager, Textile Process Specialist or Technical Operations Manager.

blocks.text: Career progression depends on specialization, industry experience, technical competence and further training.
Diploma programmes commonly take three years after Class 10, although duration and curriculum vary by institution and programme.

items: Release Material to the Next Process

blocks.text: The precise workflow varies by textile segment. Dyeing, finishing and chemical processing require additional process controls, environmental procedures and chemical-safety practices.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Fabric Defect Identification Catalogue
Collect permitted fabric samples or use reference images to document defects such as holes, stains, uneven weaving, broken yarns and colour variation.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: fabric inspection, defect classification and quality documentation.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Textile Material Testing Report
Conduct institution-approved tests on selected fabric samples and compare results for properties such as mass per unit area, thickness or tensile strength.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: testing procedures, measurement, results interpretation and reporting.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Textile Production Dashboard
Use Excel or Power BI to track production output, fabric rejection rates, machine downtime, rework and shift performance using sample data.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: production monitoring, data analysis and reporting.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Textile Machine Inspection Checklist
Create a supervised inspection checklist covering machine cleanliness, guards, visible wear, lubrication checks and operating observations.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: equipment awareness, preventive maintenance and safety documentation.

blocks.label: Recommended path

blocks.text: The strongest candidates combine textile-material knowledge, practical machine awareness, quality inspection and accurate production documentation. Select a clear specialization early, gain hands-on experience and build evidence of your ability to identify defects, maintain quality and support efficient production.
